title: Ranveer Singh Is Fighting Zombies. Vicky Kaushal Is Becoming a God. Bollywood's Next Bench Just Made Its Biggest Bets.
excerpt: Ranveer blocks August for the ₹300-crore zombie epic 'Pralay' — and turns producer — while Vicky surrenders 18 months to play Parashurama in 'Mahavatar'. The biggest swings aren't coming from the marquee names anymore.
body:
There's a particular kind of Bollywood ambition that doesn't announce itself with a trailer — it announces itself with a calendar. And this week, two of Hindi cinema's most magnetic leading men quietly blocked out enormous chunks of their lives for films that don't even start rolling yet. **Ranveer Singh** is taking on a zombie apocalypse. **Vicky Kaushal** is becoming a god. Neither is doing it small.

Start with Ranveer, because Ranveer is incapable of doing anything quietly. Fresh off the record-shattering run of the *Dhurandhar* franchise, the actor is set to roll cameras on **Pralay** in August 2026 — a large-scale, VFX-drenched zombie thriller that he's also co-producing under his newly minted banner, **Maa Kasam Films**. It's his debut as a producer, which means for the first time the swagger comes with a stake. Directed by **Jai Mehta** (of *Scam 1992* pedigree) and mounted on a reported ₹300-crore budget, *Pralay* is being designed as a post-apocalyptic survival epic — the kind of genre Indian cinema has flirted with but never truly committed to at this scale.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=njJgvfW3Hv8</youtube>


The casting coup here is **Kalyani Priyadarshan**, the South Indian star whose fantasy blockbuster *Lokah: Chapter 1 – Chandra* closed at a thunderous ₹303.86 crore worldwide. She's making her Bollywood debut opposite Ranveer, and the whisper is that he personally convinced her to come aboard.



> **"And yet, per the production, "FWICE's unlawful directive has had no impact on the film whatsoever." Translation: the zombies are still coming in August, controversy or no controversy."**


> "Ranveer and Jai have been in continuous discussions and have firmly locked the script. The project has already moved into pre-production." — an insider, to NDTV


![South Indian — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Tirumala_090615.jpg/3840px-Tirumala_090615.jpg)


That clarification matters, because *Pralay* has not had a frictionless few weeks. Ranveer is in the middle of a genuine industry storm — his exit from **Don 3** triggered a non-cooperation directive from the Federation of Western India Cine Employees, with Excel Entertainment reportedly seeking ₹45 crore in compensation. And yet, per the production, "FWICE's unlawful directive has had no impact on the film whatsoever." Translation: the zombies are still coming in August, controversy or no controversy. Classic Ranveer — turn the volume up, never down.

Then there's **Vicky Kaushal**, who is approaching ambition from the opposite temperament: not loud, but total. The *Chhaava* and *Love & War* star has reportedly **blocked off 18 entire months** for **Mahavatar**, the mythological epic from *Stree* and *Bala* director **Amar Kaushik**, produced by the supernatural-universe juggernaut **Maddock Films**. Kaushal plays **Parashurama**, the axe-wielding warrior avatar of Vishnu — and the first-look poster, which showed a fierce, almost unrecognisable Vicky, sent the internet into a tailspin.

The commitment is the story. Filming begins in January 2027 and runs a full year, wrapping by December 2027, and for that entire stretch Kaushal has consciously decided to take on nothing else. No squeezed-in side projects (a small one before January remains a faint maybe), no parallel shoots, no divided attention. He's treating *Mahavatar* as a once-in-a-lifetime role and behaving accordingly — locking his look, his body, and his calendar to a single character. In an era of actors juggling four films a year, that kind of monk-like focus is its own flex.

What's quietly thrilling about both moves is what they signal about where the big swings are coming from. The reigning superstars — your Khans, your Kumars — built the temple. But it's this slightly younger, hungrier bench that's now mounting the genuinely risky, genre-bending spectacles: a homegrown zombie franchise, a mythological avatar saga designed to rival anything Hollywood puts up. Maddock, fresh off the runaway success of *Stree* and *Munjya*, is betting its supernatural goodwill on a serious mythological universe. Ranveer is betting his own money. These aren't safe choices. They're the choices stars make when they want to be remembered for more than their dance numbers.

For the diaspora, both are tailor-made for the big screen. *Pralay's* dystopian world-building and *Mahavatar's* mythological grandeur are exactly the kind of VFX-forward spectacle that plays gorgeously in IMAX halls from Jersey City to Wembley — and both will almost certainly arrive with multi-language releases aimed squarely at pan-India and overseas audiences. The wait, admittedly, is long: *Pralay* shoots from August, *Mahavatar* not until 2027. But the most interesting films are often the ones being built right now, in the quiet, while everyone else is watching the weekend box office.

Two leading men. Two enormous gambles. One betting on the end of the world, the other on the dawn of a god. Bollywood's next chapter isn't being written by the men at the top of the marquee — it's being written by the ones willing to disappear into a role for eighteen months, or stake their own banner on a genre nobody's cracked. That's the kind of ambition worth watching.
